newsitem.title: USA: FORECAST--U.S. July trade gap wider after June dip.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST--U.S. July trade gap wider after June dip.

text.p: The U.S. trade deficit likely expanded in July after a huge drop in June, bolstered by renewed domestic demand for imported goods and a recent runup in oil prices, analysts said Monday.
Japan's nascent economic recovery continues to rein in the U.S.-Japan shortfall, but weak demand for U.S. goods in China, Canada and Europe hampers further progress, analysts said.
"The recovery in Japan actually looks pretty good, but Canada, our number one trading partner, is doing very poorly," said Peter Jaquette, senior economist at WEFA Group.
